planting.note: Press offsets onto very well-drained, gritty, lean soil in spring or fall; this large-rosette cultivar colors best with full sun and minimal soil depth.

directions: Grow 'Killer' in gritty, sharply drained, lean soil in full sun, where its large 5-inch rosettes develop dramatic near-black purple-red coloring with contrasting blue-green tips that shift with the seasons. Like other sempervivums it is monocarpic — each large hen dies after flowering — but the surrounding chicks quickly fill in the gap, so leave several offsets in place rather than removing all of them. It thrives on neglect and rots quickly in heavy or waterlogged soil, so raised beds, troughs, and rock crevices are ideal sites. Afternoon shade in the hottest summer climates can help preserve rosette color and prevent scorching.

planting.note: Press offsets into very well-drained, gravelly soil in full sun; cold snaps intensify this cultivar's rosy-red coloring rather than damaging it.

directions: 'Red Beauty' produces medium, open rosettes of grey-green leaves tipped in blood-red that flush to a bright cerise in cool fall and winter weather, giving the planting genuine cold-season interest. Grow in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun — strong light is essential for the cultivar to develop its best color contrast. It spreads by stolon-borne offsets that can be left to form a tidy cluster or detached and transplanted elsewhere. Light pink summer flower clusters appear on a central stalk from a rosette that then dies, leaving offsets to carry on the clump; excellent for troughs, walls, and gravel gardens.

planting.note: Plant nursery starts in spring once soil has warmed, in gritty, fast-draining soil; this Wheels of Wonder series selection is bred for larger, more saturated flower color than the species.

directions: Part of the Wheels of Wonder breeding series, 'Fire Wonder' is a mat-forming succulent groundcover that produces an unusually intense flush of fiery red-orange-coral daisy-form flowers from early summer through fall, with a more compact and floriferous habit than older ice plant selections. Grow in full sun in lean, gritty, sharply drained soil — good drainage is the single most important factor for winter survival, since these succulents rot quickly in wet or heavy clay. Water sparingly once established; overwatering promotes rot and reduces flowering. Excellent for hot, dry slopes, gravel gardens, and rock wall crevices where its trailing stems can spill over edges.

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; deadhead spent stems to keep the fuchsia-carmine display going into early summer.

directions: This German-bred cultivar (its name translated from 'Düsseldorfer Stolz') forms a tight, evergreen tuft of narrow, bluish-green grass-like leaves topped from mid-spring through early summer with round, carmine-red to fuchsia flower balls on wiry stems that stand well above the foliage. It is more compact and heavier-blooming than the wild species, making it a strong choice for tight edging along paths, rock garden pockets, and seaside plantings. Grow in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun — rich or constantly moist soil causes floppy growth and crown rot. It tolerates salt spray, wind, and drought once established, and benefits from division every three to four years to maintain vigor and bloom density.

planting.note: Plant in dry, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; avoid rich loam or clay, which cause the tight cushion habit to open up and flop.

directions: 'Splendens' forms a dense, mounded tuft of dark green, grass-like evergreen foliage and sends up slender 6-8 inch stalks bearing round clusters of deep rose-pink flowers in profuse mid-to-late spring bloom, with scattered summer rebloom. It is a durable, low-maintenance choice for edging, rock gardens, and dry streambeds, and its compact size also suits pots and alpine troughs. Grow in dry, sharply drained soil in full sun; it is not suited to rich, moisture-retentive loam or clay, which weaken the tight cushion form. Once established it tolerates drought, wind, and poor soil with ease and needs only occasional deadheading to look tidy.

planting.note: Plant in infertile, dry, well-drained soil in full sun for the tightest habit and heaviest white bloom.

directions: This white-flowered sport of sea thrift forms a dense, mounded tuft of narrow, dark green, grass-like evergreen leaves and produces round, pom-pom-like clusters of pure white flowers on slender stalks from late spring into early summer, with sporadic rebloom through summer. It is a charming, easy-care edging plant for walks, borders, and rock gardens, and its white flowers pair well as a cooling accent among the pinks and purples of other rock garden perennials. Grow in infertile, dry, sharply drained soil in full sun; it is fully hardy through severe winters and needs no winter protection. The cut flower heads hold their form well and can be used in fresh arrangements.

planting.note: Set out young plants in early spring in lean, well-drained, alkaline to neutral soil in full to part sun; this compact series stays tidier and more mounded than the straight species.

directions: The Little Treasure series was bred for a more compact, mounding habit than typical Arabis caucasica, forming dense cushions of gray-green foliage that stay tighter and less sprawling in small rock garden spaces, troughs, and edging strips. Plants bear masses of small four-petaled flowers in early spring, with color selections available in addition to white. Grow in lean, well-drained, gritty soil in full to part sun; overly rich or wet soil leads to loose, floppy growth and reduced hardiness. Shear back lightly after flowering to maintain the compact mounded form and encourage dense regrowth for the following season.

planting.note: Plant divisions in average, gritty, well-drained soil in sun to part sun; foliage color is best where summers aren't excessively hot and humid.

directions: 'Variegata' offers the same fragrant white spring flowers as the species but adds striking cream-edged foliage that provides ornamental interest well beyond the bloom season, brightening rock walls and edging beds even when not in flower. Grow in average, gritty, lean, rocky, well-drained soil in sun to part sun; some afternoon shade helps preserve crisp variegation and prevent leaf scorch in hot climates. It is semi-evergreen and drought tolerant once established, and attracts bees during its spring bloom period. Trim lightly after flowering to keep the mat neat and encourage fresh variegated growth.

planting.note: Plant in very well-drained, lean, alkaline soil in full sun; shear hard after bloom to maintain a compact, floriferous mound.

directions: 'Whitewell Gem' is one of the oldest and most reliable Aubrieta selections, valued for larger flowers and more vigorous growth than seed-strain aubrieta, producing masses of reddish-purple to deep violet blooms with small yellow eyes over a compact, rounded mound of green foliage in spring. Grow in very well-drained, lean, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; it struggles in hot, humid summer climates and performs best where summers stay relatively cool. Shear the plant back hard immediately after flowering to prevent the center from opening up and going bare, and to encourage a tidy, dense regrowth. Excellent cascading over rock walls or as edging along a sunny path; it attracts bees and butterflies.

planting.note: Sow or transplant into well-drained, alkaline, gritty soil in full sun to part shade; give room to trail, since it can spread widely once established.

directions: 'Royal Blue' bears a profusion of rich violet-blue, four-petaled flowers over soft, gray-green, semi-evergreen foliage from March through June, and is especially prized for cascading down walls, gravel paths, and container edges where its long, sprawling stems can spill freely. Grow in well-draining, alkaline soil in full sun; it tolerates partial shade but blooms less heavily there. It thrives as a waterwise perennial once established, needing little supplemental water beyond an establishment period, and is a strong candidate for gravel gardens, alpine beds, and rock wall crevices. Cut plants back by roughly half after the main spring flush to keep growth dense and to encourage a tidier summer habit.

planting.note: Plant in lean, well-drained, alkaline soil in full sun to part shade; part of the vigorous Cascade breeding series bred for extra-long trailing stems.

directions: A strong-growing, mat-forming member of the Cascade breeding series, 'Red Cascade' produces single, deep magenta-red flowers in a dense spring flush over gray-green, semi-evergreen foliage, with noticeably longer, more trailing stems than older aubrieta strains. This habit makes it especially effective spilling over the tops of retaining walls, raised beds, and window boxes rather than staying in a tight mound. Grow in lean, well-drained, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun to light shade; it performs poorly in hot, humid summer regions and prefers cooler summer climates. Shear back by about half after the main bloom period to keep growth compact and encourage rebloom later in the season.

planting.note: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun to light shade; shear hard after the first flush to encourage rebloom.

directions: 'Snow Tip' is a vigorous, low, mounding white-flowered selection of rock soapwort, smothering itself in snowy white, five-petaled blooms for months beginning in mid-spring — a striking contrast to the pink-flowered species. It is ideal tumbling over walls, filling gaps between large stepping stones, and cascading from containers or troughs. Grow in well-drained, lean soil in full sun to light shade; it can struggle and thin out in hot, humid summer conditions, so afternoon shade is worthwhile in warmer zones. Shear the plant back hard immediately after the main spring bloom to keep it compact, encourage a tidy mat, and promote a possible second flush of flowers.

planting.note: Plant in chalky, loamy, or sandy well-drained soil in full sun; its dwarf habit suits small trough and crevice plantings better than the species.

directions: 'Rubra Compacta' is a dwarf, semi-evergreen selection of rock soapwort forming a tight, glossy green mound noticeably smaller than the species, smothered in loose clusters of deep pink to ruby-red flowers through late spring and into early summer. Its compact scale makes it a good fit for smaller rock garden pockets, alpine troughs, and crevice plantings where the standard species would spread too aggressively. Grow in well-drained chalk, loam, or sandy soil in full sun; good drainage is essential, as it is prone to crown rot in heavy or waterlogged ground. Shear back after flowering to maintain its dense, tidy habit and encourage renewed compact growth.
